# Lenz 0.0.17 beta

This release reworks the menus and popups of Lenz Diff and Lenz Code, in the GUI and the terminal apps (PR #55).

- Menus, palettes, pickers, tooltips and dialogs share one raised look in both windows: a visible shadow, rounded corners and a rounded highlighted row. The highlighted row now shows in every built-in theme; in several dark themes it was within 4% of the popup's background.
- The Diff command palette lists group and shortcut in aligned columns and highlights the typed words where they matched.
- Lenz Code's full command menu (F10) lists every command under its menu's heading (File, File › New, View › Terminal…) instead of catalog order. Settings show a check mark when on instead of "(on)" / "(off)".
- Lenz Code's Language Server popup shows Setup and Indexing as headings; they looked like commands that could not be selected.
- Popup lists that overflow show a scrollbar thumb. Lenz Code's explorer and Diff's Files list get a scrollbar: in the GUI the thumb drags and a press on its track jumps there; in the terminal it shows the position.
- In Lenz Code, a drag selection held past the top or bottom of the text scrolls it and extends the selection. In the terminal this needs pointer movement, because terminals report a held button only when it moves.
- Terminal context menus open at the pointer, sized to their rows; Shift-F10 still centres them. Lenz Code's terminal context menu no longer wraps a long label under the next row.
- Dialogs that must be answered shade the window behind them.

Popup scrollbars and the terminal file-list scrollbars show the position only; the wheel and the keys scroll as before.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. No benchmark comparison with 0.0.16 was made: the changes paint popups, not the text or diff paths.

The new look was checked by screenshot on a private display in Catppuccin Mocha, Light and Tokyo Night, at a narrow window and a 60-column terminal. Native AppKit/macOS interaction and physical-display behavior remain unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.16](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.16...v0.0.17).
